title: kanban rm refuses a card whose worktree and branch are both gone
body:
`foreman kanban rm <id>` refuses a card whose worktree folder AND card/<id> branch are both gone, even though no unmerged work is left to protect. Today the only way out is hand-editing the card JSON to delete its "worktree" key.

Repro: a worktree card with a commit ahead of base, then
  git worktree remove .foreman/worktrees/<id> && git branch -D card/<id>
  foreman kanban rm <id>
fails with:
  foreman kanban: card <id>: cannot verify its worktree (fatal: ambiguous argument 'main...card/<id>': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.); retry or discard it first
Grep that message to find the guard.

Fix: when the branch does not exist (check with git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/card/<id>, don't parse error text), treat it as nothing to lose and delete the card. Keep refusing on any other git failure, and keep the existing dirty/ahead refusals for a branch that does exist.

Acceptance:
- New test: card with worktree metadata, tree folder and branch both missing -> rm succeeds and the card file is gone.
- Existing rm guard tests (dirty tree, ahead of base) still refuse.
- docs/kanban-board.md updated if it describes rm's guard.

Possibly related, not confirmed: the board's discard also failed on the same card (blocked, unclaimed, clean, +1 -2) before the branch was deleted. The symptom wasn't recorded, so don't chase it unless the same code path is obviously at fault.

Gate: cargo build --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent; cargo fmt --check
